firstTwoSpecced.title: Harden the watcher to a multi-RPC FallbackProvider (list-based RPC env), Sepolia + mainnet
firstTwoSpecced.plan: 1) In backend/config.mjs, add list-based RPC parsing alongside the existing single-RPC envs (config.mjs:60,71): for each chain accept a comma-separated env (e.g. MAINNET_RPCS / SEPOLIA_RPCS) and fall back to the existing single MAINNET_RPC/SEPOLIA_RPC, then to the hardcoded public default. Expose cfg.rpcs as a non-empty string[] on each chain config object (keep cfg.rpc as rpcs[0] for back-compat). Keys stay backend-only (lint G5 already blocks keyed URLs in frontend/). 2) In backend/watcher.mjs, change provider construction at line 300 from `new ethers.JsonRpcProvider(cfg.rpc)` to a helper buildProvider(cfg) that: if cfg.rpcs.length===1 returns a single JsonRpcProvider configured with { staticNetwork: true, batchMaxCount: 3 } (mirror frontend + monitor.mjs:63); if >1 returns a FallbackProvider over JsonRpcProvider instances each with staticNetwork + a priority, constructed with { quorum: 1 } so a single healthy provider serves reads. 3) Make buildProvider injectable: accept an optional providers param in startWatcher (currently builds provider inline at ~297-304) so the unit test can pass fakes — thread it the same way the existing injectable sleep is threaded for getLogsWithRetry. 4) Do NOT change checkpoint discipline: indexChain must still leave the checkpoint un-advanced on a window that fails on ALL providers (no-skip invariant). 5) Leave Sepolia on the free publicnode default if no SEPOLIA_RPCS provided (a Sepolia key is the owner-funded follow-up noted in BACKLOG.md:23) — but the FallbackProvider plumbing must still work when given a 2-entry list of public endpoints.
firstTwoSpecced.tests: Extend test/backend/readModelAndIndexer.test.js (child-process + isolated temp DB pattern already in the file). Add a test that builds a fake provider LIST: provider[0].getLogs and getBlockNumber throw; provider[1] returns a head and one BondCreated-style log. Call indexChain (the same entry the existing resilience tests drive) with the injected providers and assert: (a) the bond row is written to the DB (rows came from provider[1]); (b) the index checkpoint advanced past the window. Add a second assertion that when ALL providers throw on a window, the checkpoint does NOT advance (no-skip invariant). Run via `npx hardhat test` (mocha picks up test/backend/*) — these are pure Node, no RPC. The test must assert failover actually occurred (row present from the 2nd provider), not merely that construction succeeded.
firstTwoSpecced.doneWhen: `npx hardhat test` green including the new failover + no-skip assertions; `node scripts/lint-guardrails.mjs` exits 0 with G5 still clean (no keyed URL in frontend/); `node scripts/monitor.mjs` green; the watcher constructs a FallbackProvider when given >1 RPC and a hardened single provider otherwise; metrics.json rcaOpenGaps decremented 10->9 with gap #1 marked resolved in BACKLOG.md.

firstTwoSpecced.title: Wire a `capabilities` map into the scoreboard via a Playwright post-run JSON aggregator
firstTwoSpecced.plan: 1) Confirm the journey test titles carry stable codes (poster-flows/judge-flows/challenger-flows already use C*/E*/D* codes per the data; grep each .spec.js to build the authoritative title->flag map). Define the target flag set from CHARTER 3 + BACKLOG D: createBond, becomeJudge, challengeAndRule, concede, withdraw, drainRefunds, claimTimeout. 2) Add scripts/aggregate-capabilities.mjs: run/consume `playwright test --project local --reporter=json` output (write the JSON report to a temp path, e.g. via PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_NAME or the json reporter file option in playwright.config.js), parse each spec's status, and for each known flag set true ONLY if its mapped test(s) have status 'passed'. A test that is skipped/host-gated (several live-* specs test.skip on baseURL) maps to absent/false, never true. 3) Merge the resulting map into docs/autoloop/metrics.json under `capabilities` (read-modify-write, preserve other keys; bump `updated`). The aggregator is the ONLY writer of capability flags, keyed to the passing test, so the loop can't fake-green (CHARTER: gaming a metric is a failure). 4) scoreboard.mjs already renders capabilities (lines 67-70) — verify it prints the populated map; no change needed there unless formatting. 5) Wire the aggregator into scripts/e2e-docker.sh (or a thin npm script) so it runs after the `local` e2e project completes.
firstTwoSpecced.tests: (a) Aggregator unit/smoke: feed aggregate-capabilities.mjs a synthetic Playwright JSON report fixture (one passing journey, one failing, one skipped) and assert the merged map sets the passing flag true, the failing flag false, the skipped flag absent/false — pure Node, no browser. (b) Integration: run `./scripts/e2e-docker.sh --project local` then the aggregator, and assert `node scripts/scoreboard.mjs --json` shows capabilities non-empty with at least createBond=true (the create journey already passes locally). (c) Anti-gaming check: on a throwaway branch, deliberately break one journey, re-run, assert that flag flips to false on the next aggregation, then revert (never leave main red, per CHARTER).
firstTwoSpecced.doneWhen: `node scripts/scoreboard.mjs --json` reports a non-empty `capabilities` map populated from real passing `local` journeys; metrics.json `capabilities` is no longer {}; the aggregator refuses to set a flag true for a skipped/failed test (verified by the synthetic-report unit test); `./scripts/e2e-docker.sh --project local` stays green and the aggregation step runs after it; lint + hardhat + monitor gates unchanged and green.

sequencingNotes: "Ordered by (UX leverage x feasibility) with dependencies and the CHARTER's de-risk-first principle. WAVE 1 (de-risk everything, no dependencies): B1 (watcher FallbackProvider — the #1 RCA gap; keeps every downstream page/email alive through an RPC outage) and H1 (capabilities scoreboard — without it the loop has NO behavioral progress signal to gate on; CHARTER 3 calls journeys the primary signal). These are the two specced-in-full items and can run in parallel (disjoint files: backend vs test/infra). WAVE 2 (high-leverage frontend on the already-built backend, all pure-frontend, no contract deploy): A1 staleness banner (closes RCA #2, tiny, depends on B1's reliable backend), then B3 indexer-first bond detail (closes RCA #9, the most-visited page; unblocks the detail-page UX cluster). WAVE 3 (detail-page UX cluster, all depend on B3 painting from the indexer): A2 status timeline + why-no-action (unblocks A4/A5 by giving them phase data), then A3 USD consistency, A4 refunds affordance, A5 lifecycle banner, A6 notifications (depends on A1's meta-aware fetch plumbing). WAVE 4 (deeper backend reliability, parallelizable with Wave 3): B2 dead-letter/auto-recovery and B4 last-tick-age SLO. WAVE 5 (v0.7 contract, testnet-first, LAST per CHARTER): C1 pending-cap (smallest, near-trivial one-line gate change that removes a live revert-on-submit and fixes a UI/contract divergence) before C2 credit-ledger (largest surface; depends on C1 being the v0.7 cut and on A4's refund UX existing to replace). Three CUT items from the skeptic scores are dropped: 'Payout event' (redundant — every disbursement is closed-form derivable; do the derived ledger in the read-model instead), 'demote judge flow' (already shipped — would be cosmetic churn), and 'staging deploy-readiness gate' (guards a write-suite that doesn't exist). Three DEFERRED-but-not-dropped items (optimistic-updating half of A.2, concedeAll, single-tx exit, decouple-concession, reorg detection, live-sepolia fixture, staging write-journey port, indexer dual-verify SLO, idempotent journeys) are intentionally below the 12-item line: most are either change-for-change against a non-problem, blocked on owner Sepolia funding, or deliverable frontend-only without their proposed contract change. Stop-criteria reminder: if 3 consecutive iterations make no progress, regenerate this backlog."
